title: FixedBatchConfidence.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained convex quadratic minimization: f(x)=½ E[⟨a,x−u⟩²], with minimum f(u)=0. The covariance may be singular; no positive lower eigenvalue or strong convexity is required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns g(x,a)=⟨a,x−u⟩a using a fresh IID sample. This is an unbiased gradient of f. Only the gradient vector is returned; neither the sample a nor a function value is provided. L and x0 are public; R, ε, δ, u, and the sampling distribution are hidden.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is exactly two-dimensional real Euclidean space with its standard inner product.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Realizable least squares with bounded features: ‖a‖²≤L almost surely. Every sample loss has the common minimizer u, so stochastic gradients vanish at u. Sample Hessians aaᵀ have operator norm at most L, and f is L-smooth. The gradient noise is state-dependent, with E‖g(x,a)−∇f(x)‖²≤2Lf(x); no globally uniform variance bound is assumed. The initial point satisfies ‖x0−u‖≤R. Valid parameters obey L,R,ε>0 and 0<δ<1.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output must be measurable and satisfy f(output)−f(u)≤ε outside the allowed failure event, for some global minimizer u. No particular iterate or averaging rule is prescribed.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: P(f(output)−f(u)>ε)≤δ, equivalently success probability at least 1−δ. In Template.Convergence, this probability includes algorithm randomness and oracle randomness.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is realizable population least-squares minimization with bounded IID features, stochastic gradients, and a high-probability objective-gap target, an established stochastic optimization formulation. Least-squares stochastic approximation is treated in [Bach and Moulines (2013)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2013/file/7fe1f8abaad094e0b5cb1b01d712f708-Paper.pdf). No proved results or extracted budgets were supplied, so no complexity comparison is reported.

descriptionHtml:
Confidence Guarantees for Quadratic Minimization

We consider minimizing f(x)=12Ea∼ν[⟨a,x−x⋆⟩2] over x∈R2, where ν is a probability distribution and x⋆∈R2 is an unknown minimizer. In the Euclidean norm, ∥a∥2≤L holds ν-almost surely for L>0, and a given point x0 satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R for R>0. Each oracle call at x returns ⟨a,x−x⋆⟩a using a fresh independent sample from ν. For ε>0 and δ∈(0,1), the goal is a measurable output x¯ satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε with probability at least 1−δ.

The optimization problem is minx∈R2f(x). We use the standard Euclidean inner product and its induced norm. The algorithm receives only L and x0; the parameters R, ε, and δ may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Population quadratic and initial distance). There exist a Borel probability distribution ν on R2 and a point x⋆∈R2 such that f(x)=12Ea∼ν[⟨a,x−x⋆⟩2],x∈R2,∥a∥2≤L,ν-almost surely,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. In particular, f is a convex quadratic and f(x⋆)=0 is its global minimum.

Assumption 2 (Independent stochastic gradient samples). The sample sequence (ak)k≥0 consists of measurable, mutually independent random vectors with common distribution ν. It is independent of the algorithm’s randomness. At call k, a query x∈R2 receives g(x,ak)=⟨ak,x−x⋆⟩ak.

Queries may be made anywhere in R2. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯∈R2 must be measurable and satisfy P(f(x¯)−f(x⋆)>ε)≤δ, where P is the joint law of the sample sequence and the algorithm’s independent randomness.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.FixedBatchConfidence

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Space := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

structure Public where
  L : ℝ
  x0 : Space

structure Params extends Public where
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  δ : ℝ

structure Model (q : Params) (p : ProbabilityMeasure Space)
    (f : Space → ℝ) (u : Space) : Prop where
  bounded : ∀ᵐ a ∂(p : Measure Space), ‖a‖ ^ 2 ≤ q.L
  radius : ‖q.x0 - u‖ ≤ q.R
  population : ∀ x, f x = ∫ a, ⟪a, x - u⟫ ^ 2 / 2 ∂(p : Measure Space)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance _ := Space → ℝ
  Query _ := Space
  Reply _ := Space
  Output _ := Space
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧ 0 < q.δ ∧ q.δ < 1
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (p : ProbabilityMeasure Space) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → Space)) (u : Space),
      Model q p f u ∧
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → Space) => ξ k)
        (p : Measure Space) (P : Measure (ℕ → Space)) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => Space
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, x) a => ⟪a, x - u⟫ • a }
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ ∃ u, IsMinOn f Set.univ u ∧
      (P : Measure _) {ω | q.ε < f (output ω) - f u} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal q.δ

end LongTails.Setups.FixedBatchConfidence
